items.summary: Agent-autoloop is an open-source automation middle platform designed to address the issue of command line AI assistants (like Claude Code, Codex) not being able to run automatically in the background. It allows these AI agents to automatically handle tasks, follow through, and exit after completing a round, only notifying the user for decisions when needed. It supports macOS and Linux, requires Node 24, Git, curl, and a logged-in command line AI assistant, and is suitable for developers who frequently use command line AI for coding or automation but prefer not to constantly monitor the terminal.

It is available as a Windows application requiring Windows 10 or 11, an NVIDIA RTX 20-series or newer GPU with 8 GB VRAM, Python 3.11, Git, and roughly 45 GB of free disk space. The setup process downloads about 15–20 GB and takes 30–60 minutes. For the language model, an OpenRouter API key or Ollama with a model of at least 27B parameters is needed. items.title: hermes-voice
items.description: Talk to a Hermes Agent profile through Home Assistant Assist
items.summary: The sources indicate that the Hermes-Voice integration allows Home Assistant to communicate with the Hermes Agent server over WebSocket, enabling Hermes to function as a conversation agent within Home Assistant's Assist pipeline. The integration registers a Home Assistant Assist conversation agent (`HermesConversationAgent`) on the `Platform.CONVERSATION` platform and handles both incoming `assist_query` and outgoing `assist_response` WebSocket messages. Hermes appears in the Preferred conversation agent selector under Settings → Voice assistants after setup. The integration does not replace the bundled Hermes integration and existing skills should continue to work. The pipeline handshake succeeds but conversation queries time out after 45 seconds if the Hermes Agent server does not handle the required message types.

items.title: devvm

items.summary: devvm is a free and open-source tool that provides an isolated sandbox VM for every project, equipped with the project’s toolchain and ready for coding. Coding agents like Claude Code and Codex can run within the VM. Keelen, on the other hand, offers a single-use, network-isolated VM for each coding task, with no persistent disk and no internet access except for GitHub and registries. Google’s AI coding agent Jules operates asynchronously in Google Cloud VMs, using AI to fix or update code while developers focus on other tasks.

items.title: uni-robot-agent

items.summary: uni-robot-agent is an MIT-licensed open-source harness for robot-use agents, developed by Tsinghua University and UC Berkeley. It provides a unified tool interface and feedback across environments, enabling robot-use agents to control robots by calling tools for perception and motion rather than outputting joint commands. It runs agents through Codex or Claude Code runtimes or its own Python SDK, and records each episode for replay in a standardized format. The project aims to democratize robot-use agents by providing an open harness with shared tools across environments, supporting efficient experience collection for open models, and making simulation and real-world experience easier to combine for training.

items.summary: The sources provide information on three memory servers: Mem0, Cognee, and Supermemory. items.title: adobe-air-desktop-tool
items.description: Adobe AIR SDK for Windows: Build Cross-Platform Desktop Apps with AJAX, HTML, and Flash
items.summary: Adobe AIR SDK allows developers to create applications on various desktop platforms, enabling them to build applications tailored to a specific host platform or create universal.air installers that work with the shared AIR runtime. It supports the development of applications on desktop and mobile platforms using ActionScript, Flex, HTML, and JavaScript. The latest stable release is 51.3.1.1, released on February 12, 2026. The runtime supports installable applications on Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, and other operating systems.

items.title: ai-app-builder-open
items.description: Open-source AI app builder for full-stack Next.js apps with hosting and auth
items.summary: The ai-app-builder-open is an open-source AI app builder that turns a prompt into a full-stack Next.js web app with built-in hosting, sandbox, database, and authentication. It supports various providers for authentication, payments, and databases. The builder runs on Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS 4. It offers features like one-click deploy, live URL, chat panel, live preview, integrated Monaco code editor, managed database, secrets management, one-click hosting, custom domains, bidirectional GitHub sync, version history with rollback, live server logs, isolated sandboxes, and a visual git-diff viewer. The builder is self-hosted and no-code, offering an alternative to Lovable, Bolt, and Replit.
